Q: In Python under Unix, ask for interactive terminal input but avoid stdout A:

In Python (Linux version) you can open tty like so:

tty = open("/dev/tty", "r")
# do something ...
tty.close()

The Pythonic way would be:

with open("/dev/tty", "r") as tty:
    # do something

Since your code needs to read and write from/to tty, we need 2 objects for difference purposes:

with open("/dev/tty", "r") as tin:
    with open("/dev/tty", "w") as tout:
        tout.write("enter data please: ")
        tout.flush()
        data = tin.readline().strip()
        tout.write(f"data is: {data}")

So if your function user_answers_ok_on_tty() needs to only interact with tty, it could be something like this:

def user_answers_ok_on_tty(prompt: str, line: str) -> bool:
    with open("/dev/tty", "r") as tin:
        with open("/dev/tty", "w") as tout:
            tout.write(f"{line.strip()}\n")
            tout.write(f"{prompt}: ")
            tout.flush()
            answer = tin.readline().strip().lower()
            return answer == "ok"

ok = user_answers_ok_on_tty("please answer ok or not", "anything goes")
print(ok)

The output should be True if then given answer is "ok".

Q: Spring Boot - Web vs Webflux for RESTAPI A:
  1. Currently, is Webflux still buggy? No, webflux is reactive approach of programming. It may be hard to understand for people who has more experience on old MVC way.
  2. Is coding (using Kotlin) on Webflux actually very different from Web? I use Kotlin and have done some demo projects and both Web and Webflux seem very similar to me. It is similar from coding side but run flow of the code is different. Meaning catching responses from DB or any othor call works little bit different then regular older ways.
  3. Currently, is debugging on Webflux still so difficult? No If so, and thinking in the long run, would you NOT use Webflux because of this? Webflux may require more fine tuning on threads but after all it is same thing in different approach, if you are willing to do that way, go for it because webflux mature enough, you can learn and share.
  4. Is Webflux a direct improvement/upgrade from Web? No If not, can you tell me why? Because there is no proof I have seen so far it is better than non reactive approach. In what cases would you use Web instead of Webflux, given that Webflux uses resources more efficiently? Mostly I would use Web instead of webflux, then if I am having heavy load I would do A/B tests and compare performance which can be affected from DB design to netwrok, webflux mainly promise better performance on heavy load, but without testing throughly I would not believe it and it changes every application and DB
  5. Does Virtual Thread from Java 21 make Web a better choice than Webflux? Maybe I read that Virtual Thread would be a "gamechanger" to Web. Is this true? They look shiny but I am not sure it will bring soo much for webflux, check here.

I have been testing webflux for a long time, I see webflux has better numbers than spring web(sometimes-check different tests on the page), but my test is only depends on json serialization, if we put in DB layer all numbers would change, app to app and design to design we should do more tests and decide after.

Q: How can I tell if a command is available in real DOS? A:

What is your actual goal? Are you trying to write a batch file for DOS, or do you want a batch file to run identically under both DOS command.com and cmd.exe? That is practically impossible. Even commands built into both work differently.

Q: Create docker volume with limited size A:

You can't limit the size of bind mounts. (unless you use quotas, which in my wasted 3ams prove to be time consuming and just not necessary compared to creating an image, as detailed below.)

Instead of limiting the storage on the bind mounts you can create an image, then mount that to the location of your bind mount.

For example, instead of:
Directory >bind mount via docker> Container

You could do:
Size limited image >mounted to directory via OS> Directory >bind mount via docker> Container

You can use commands like fallocate to create a .img (image).

Q: Explain how premultiplied alpha works A:

Excerpts from here:

Straight Alpha
The image is stored in the (R, G, B, A) format where all components are independent of each other.
…

Premultiplied Alpha
The image is stored in the (R×A, G×A, B×A, A) format where the components R, G, and B are multiplied by the transparency factor. … For optimisation purposes … it is the multiplied alpha that is used so that less mathematical operations need to be performed when overlaying transparent images.

Example
Suppose we have a render and its mask.
Let's extract the object from the scene using the mask as an alpha channel.
It looks good so far, but let's try to blur it out.
The point is that transparent pixels contain colour information, which appears when blurring. When converting to internal composer format, each colour component for transparent pixels is multiplied by 0 (i.e. pixels become black) and the artefact disappears.
